sentences.text:
Deep Kurrey vs National Highways Authority Of India on 8 May,
2024
 1
 High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur
 Order Sheet
 Wpc No. 2456 of 2024
 Deep Kurrey Versus National Highways Authority Of India
08/05/2024 Mr. Shreyansh Mehta, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Dhiraj Kumar Wankhede, Advocate for respondent no. 1.
Mr. Dilman Rati Minj, G.A. for respondent no. 2/ State.
Ms. Anmol Sharma, C.G.C. for respondents no. 3 and 4/ Uoi.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner purchased the land in question on 31.07.2021 through a registered sale deed and a Notification under Section 3(A)(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 was issued on 24.12.2021 but the name of the petitioner was not mentioned in that Notification.
He would further submit that an award has already been passed in the name of the earlier owner of the property.

He would also submit that though the amount of compensation has already been deposited by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highway in the office of the Land Acquisition Officer but the amount has not been disbursed in favour of the earlier owner.

entities.text: Ministry of Road Transport and Highway
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, he would submit that till the disposal of the present petition, a direction may be issued to the Land Acquisition Officer not to disburse the amount of compensation to anyone.
On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondents would oppose the submissions made by Mr. Mehta.

Taking into consideration the fact that the petitioner purchased the land in question prior to the date of issuance of Notification and thereafter an award was passed in favour of the earlier owner,
therefore, the amount of compensation shall not be disbursed to the earlier owner if already not disbursed till the next date of hearing.
Learned counsels appearing for the respective respondents pray for and are granted four weeks time to seek instructions.
Call this matter in the last week of June, 2024.

Sd/-
